title: The PowerToys Run window is displaying an error and cannot be displayed correctly.

judgment.rationale: The bugreport revealed a Window Walker NullReferenceException, but the thread still lacks concrete trigger steps and a current-version confirmation, so the visible broken window cannot yet be tied confidently to one plugin path.
evidence: The thread contains a screenshot and a bugreport ZIP but no textual repro steps.
The attached 2026-08-28 Run log shows a Window Walker NullReferenceException during query <li>.
The same log also shows a duplicate shortcut warning, so more than one anomaly was captured.
judgment.recommended_action: Keep the thread waiting on the reporter for the exact trigger and current-version confirmation.

fix_assessment.rationale: Diagnostics surfaced a likely plugin failure, but the issue still needs a concrete trigger description before a fix plan can be published honestly.

issue_context.summary: The diagnostic ZIP for the broken PowerToys Run window contains a Window Walker NullReferenceException and a duplicate shortcut warning, but the issue does not explain what was typed or clicked to produce the visible anomalous window.
known_information: PowerToys Run 0.100.2 from the Microsoft Store.
A screenshot attachment marks the broken window visually.
The attached Run log shows a Window Walker exception while querying <li>.
inferences: Window Walker is a plausible contributor, but the screenshot alone does not prove it is the only cause of the visible UI problem.
Because the issue is on an older build, current-version confirmation still matters.
issue_context.analysis: The first bugreport already narrowed the plugin area, so the next ask should not repeat /bugreport. It should request only the exact trigger steps and current-version confirmation.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the issue body, screenshot reference, and attached bugreport ZIP.
Reviewed log lines around the Window Walker NullReferenceException and duplicate shortcut warning.
Reviewed WindowWalker SearchController and ListRepository to confirm both anomalies map to real source locations.

information_gaps.information: The exact query text, plugin, or sequence that produces the anomalous Run window shown in the screenshot.
information_gaps.why_needed: That determines whether the visible failure is the same Window Walker code path shown in diagnostics.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Please reply with short numbered steps, including the exact text typed into PowerToys Run and whether the broken window appears immediately or only after selecting a result.

information_gaps.information: Whether the same broken window still reproduces on the latest stable PowerToys build.
information_gaps.why_needed: The current report is on 0.100.2 and later builds may already change the relevant plugin path.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Please update to the latest stable build if possible and confirm whether the same issue still reproduces with the same steps.

comment.body:
Thanks for attaching the screenshot and the bugreport ZIP. The diagnostics already point at a Window Walker exception, so the next useful evidence is narrower than another generic log request. Please provide:

1. Short numbered steps for the exact trigger, including what you typed into PowerToys Run and whether the anomalous window appears immediately or only after you select a result.
2. If possible, please update to the latest stable PowerToys build and confirm whether the same broken window still reproduces with the same steps.

That will tell us whether the visible UI failure is the same Window Walker path shown in the attached logs.

design_decision.reason: Waiting on the next discriminating reporter reply.

confidence.rationale: Diagnostics narrowed the plugin area, but the visible trigger is still under-specified.
